narrative.overview:
The app is an instrument screen. A near-black field lit by three soft washes — amber from the top left, cyan from the top right, violet from below — and on it traces in saturated hues that each mean exactly one thing: comparing, swapping, in place, pivot, probing, found, with untouched elements glowing Signal Amber. The chrome around the screen is the bezel — translucent graphite, mono-labelled — and where you are is lit in the same amber: the open category, the chosen algorithm, the selected toggle. Glow is how a trace looks on phosphor, which is why the dark theme is the reference rendering; light and high-contrast are re-tunings of the same instrument, not different products.

Density is high and deliberate: a sidebar of controls, a canvas, a readout panel, a transport bar, all on one screen, because the user is operating something and watching it at once. Everything is driven from a small set of primitives on `:root` — six hue channels, one overlay ink, a surface — and three independent axes on `<html>` (`data-theme`, `data-contrast`, `data-palette`) re-point them. Components never know which theme, contrast or palette is active.

Meaning is carried twice. Every state hue has a glyph beside it (`↔ ⇄ ✓ ◆ ◎ ★`), a fill strength, and in some views a tone, so no reading of the screen depends on hue alone.
keyCharacteristics: A near-black phosphor field with three soft radial washes (amber, cyan, violet); light theme is cool paper.
State hues named for what they mean (`--state-compare-rgb`), never for their colour; idle is Signal Amber in the default palette.
Translucent fills mixed from bare RGB channels: tinted body, solid stroke, optional glow.
JetBrains Mono for controls, values, counters and code; IBM Plex Sans for names, titles, narration and prose.
Signal Amber for the current place and the current choice: filled, with a soft glow.
A drawn trace mark, and a drawn structure glyph for each family on the landing page.
Three composable appearance axes; high contrast strips glow and thickens strokes.

rules.name: The Meaning-Not-Hue Rule
rules.body: Canvases read only `--state-*-rgb` tokens. A component never names a hue for a state; the palette decides which hue a meaning gets.

rules.name: The Lit Choice Rule
rules.body: What you have chosen is lit: a selected button, tab or menu item is filled Signal Amber with On-Amber text and a soft amber glow; a selected list row or code tab is amber text on `--primary-dim`. `--active-fill` (a neutral step) is only for toggled icon buttons such as sound and the shortcut help.

rules.name: The Second Channel Rule
rules.body: No state is shown by colour alone. A new state ships with a glyph in `stateStyle.js` and a label, or it does not ship.

rules.name: The Primitive Override Rule
rules.body: Themes, contrast and palettes redefine primitives (`--ink-rgb`, the six hue channels, `--fill-*`), never component styles. If a theme needs a component-specific rule, the primitive is missing.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Any number that changes during playback is mono with tabular figures, so the digits don't jitter as they count.

rules.name: The Projection Floor Rule
rules.body: No text below 11px, except an index mark inside a cell that is sized for it (10px).

rules.name: The Silkscreen Rule
rules.body: Capitals label a control in three words or fewer. Anything that reads as a sentence is set in sentence case.

rules.name: The No Sideways Scroll Rule
rules.body: The page never scrolls horizontally at any width. Anything wide scrolls inside its own container.

rules.name: The Droppable Glow Rule
rules.body: Glow is part of the identity on dark, but it never carries meaning on its own; canvas glows go through `--glow-alpha` so high contrast can remove them, and anything that only reads because it glows is broken.

rules.name: The Static Blur Rule
rules.body: Never transform an element that has a `backdrop-filter`; the backdrop re-blurs every frame. Panels and cards carry no blur, only overlays do.

dos: **Do** mix every new fill or border from the existing channels: `rgb(var(--state-compare-rgb) / var(--fill-mid))`, `rgb(var(--ink-rgb) / 0.08)`.
**Do** give every new state a glyph, a label and a fill strength in `stateStyle.js`.

**Do** time step-driven transitions with `var(--step-anim)` so they never outlast the gap between steps; interface motion uses `--dur-press` / `--dur-ui` / `--dur-overlay` with `--ease-out` (or `--ease-drawer` for sheets), and `--control-transition` on controls.
**Do** light a selected state in Signal Amber (filled for buttons and tabs, amber text on `--primary-dim` for rows and code tabs).
**Do** check new work in all three axes: light and dark, high contrast on and off, default and safe palette.
**Do** put every control label, value and counter in JetBrains Mono.
**Do** keep all styling in `src/index.css`, with colours defined as tokens on `:root`.
donts: **Don't** hardcode a hex or `rgb()` value in a component; a palette or theme switch will miss it. (Category accents in `categories.js` point at `var(--…)` for this reason.)
**Don't** use Signal Amber as a border flourish or for body emphasis.
**Don't** put a `backdrop-filter` on a panel or card; blur is for overlays.
**Don't** let glow or hue be the only way something reads.
**Don't** put new canvas or label text below 11px.
**Don't** let anything scroll the page sideways at any width.
**Don't** add a webfont, icon CDN or remote asset; fonts are self-hosted and the app contacts no third party.
**Don't** animate a transform on an element with `backdrop-filter`.
